newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria's Assad urges Blair to back Mideast peace.
newsitem.headline: Syria's Assad urges Blair to back Mideast peace.

text.p: Syrian President Hafez al-Assad on Saturday congratulated Britain's new Prime Minister Tony Blair and expressed hope for continued British support for the Middle East peace process.

"I hope that the government of the United Kingdom under your leadership, and within the European Union, will continue to support the cause of just and comprehensive peace in the Middle East on the basis of relevant United Nations resolutions and the principle of land for peace," Assad told blair in a cable a copy of which was obtained by Reuters.
"I express my confidence that the relations of friendship and cooperation between our two countries will further strengthen in the years ahead," the Syrian leader added.
Earlier on Saturday an official Syrian newspaper said it believed Blair would give Europe a greater role in the Middle East.
Tishreen daily said Britain and Europe have a chance to increase their influence in the peace process from the United States, the main broker of the Arab-Israeli peace talks.

"With the shrinking of the U.S. role due to the flagrant U.S. submission to Israel, the region and the world look for a more effective European role. Britain can contribute to the shaping of this role as Blair himself declared," Tishreen said.
"Britain could stand firmly in support of a just and comprehensive peace and could contribute with other European states to rescue the peace proces," it said.
The paper criticised the policy of the outgoing British Conservative Party: "Positions of the Conservatives were in fact disappointing. It was biased to Israel."

Syrian-British ties were strained under the Conservatives. Britain severed diplomatic ties with Syria in 1986 after accusing Damascus of involvement in a plot to bomb an Israeli plane flying from London.
Ties were restored in 1990 prior to the Gulf War when Syrian and British forces joined the U.S.-led multinational force that drove Iraqi troops from Kuwait after six months of occupation.
